standards_review.notes: All 9 subjects match EPMCDME-####: Description exactly (EPMCDME-15435 prefix, colon+space separator, capital sentence)
All 14 new Python files carry the Apache 2.0 header. New modules use modern type syntax and from __future__ import annotations. No untyped public functions in newly introduced code.
Central auth dependencies used in user_management_router.py. KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET flows through config (env-backed), never logged. IDP guard raises HTTP 403 without echoing credential values.

findings.title: Dockerfile.sync copies full virtual environment
findings.problem: COPY --from=builder $VIRTUAL_ENV $VIRTUAL_ENV copies the entire venv built with 'poetry install --only main -E enterprise', which includes LangChain, LiteLLM, Elasticsearch client, NATS client, and Azure Storage SDK.
findings.impact: Spec requires only SQLModel/asyncpg/httpx/pydantic-settings in the final image. Full venv triples image size and includes AI/cloud packages that must not be present in the sync container, violating the minimal attack surface requirement.
findings.recommendation: Replace the single venv COPY with a targeted install in the final stage: extract only the required packages from the lock file into a requirements-sync.txt and run 'pip install -r requirements-sync.txt' in the final stage, or use a separate Poetry project scoped to sync dependencies only.

findings.title: CronJob resources block renders null when values unset
findings.problem: {{- toYaml .Values.keycloakSync.resources | nindent 16 }} has no '| default {}' guard; when keycloakSync.resources is not set in Helm values, toYaml nil produces the string 'null' at that indentation level.
findings.impact: Helm renders structurally invalid YAML for the Job spec. kubectl apply or helm install fails at parse time; the CronJob cannot be deployed without pre-defining keycloakSync.resources in every values file.

findings.title: CronJob pod has no database environment variables
findings.problem: The CronJob env block supplies only Keycloak vars (KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_URL, KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_REALM, KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_ID, KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET) and sync flags. No POSTGRES_HOST, POSTGRES_PORT, POSTGRES_DB, POSTGRES_USER, or POSTGRES_PASSWORD are provided, and there is no envFrom block.
findings.impact: entrypoint._validate_env() checks for POSTGRES_HOST and raises SystemExit(1) if missing; the sync pod fails immediately on every scheduled invocation. The CronJob is completely non-functional as deployed from this template.
findings.recommendation: Add database env entries or an envFrom: secretRef/configMapRef block covering all POSTGRES_* vars required by the entrypoint (_REQUIRED_ENV_VARS includes POSTGRES_HOST; the DB client also needs POSTGRES_PORT, POSTGRES_DB, POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_PASSWORD).

findings.title: CronJob lacks activeDeadlineSeconds
findings.problem: The job spec has no activeDeadlineSeconds. If the sync hangs (Keycloak slow, advisory lock never released, DB unresponsive), the pod runs indefinitely.
findings.impact: concurrencyPolicy: Forbid causes all subsequent scheduled invocations to be skipped for the entire lifespan of the hung pod. Sync effectively stops for the cluster with no alertable failure.
findings.recommendation: Add activeDeadlineSeconds: 300 (or a configurable Helm value) to the job spec to bound the maximum run duration and ensure the CronJob can self-recover.

findings.title: KEYCLOAK_SYNC_SCHEDULE config var is dead code
findings.problem: KEYCLOAK_SYNC_SCHEDULE is declared in config.py but the entrypoint is a one-shot process (not a scheduler), and the CronJob template draws its schedule exclusively from .Values.keycloakSync.schedule, never from this env var.
findings.impact: Operators who set KEYCLOAK_SYNC_SCHEDULE expecting to override the CronJob schedule will find their configuration silently ignored. The presence of the var in config.py creates false documentation.
findings.recommendation: Either remove KEYCLOAK_SYNC_SCHEDULE from config.py and document that the schedule is Helm-only, or add a comment in config.py explaining that this var is informational and the active schedule is set in the Helm values file.

findings.title: Advisory lock ID non-deterministic across pods due to PYTHONHASHSEED
findings.problem: _LOCK_ID = hash('keycloak_sync_coordinator') & 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF uses Python's built-in hash(), which is randomized per process by PYTHONHASHSEED. Two concurrent sync pods each compute a different lock ID.
findings.impact: The pods do not contend on the same PostgreSQL advisory lock and can run simultaneously. Concurrent runs produce duplicate user creates, double budget syncs, and conflicting membership mutations. The concurrency-exclusion design is completely ineffective in multi-pod deployments.
findings.recommendation: Replace hash() with a fixed hardcoded integer constant distinct from the migration coordinator's 7734269302, e.g. _LOCK_ID = 0x4B435359_4E4300 or any stable literal. Never derive a lock ID from a Python hash() call.

findings.title: Empty-email early return breaks 2-tuple unpack in caller
findings.problem: _reconcile_user returns a bare dict (counts) when email is empty (line 67), but returns a 2-tuple (counts, db_user) on every other path. run() at line 206 always unpacks: counts, db_user = await self._reconcile_user(...), raising ValueError for any KC user record without an email.
findings.impact: Every emailless KC user is caught by the outer except, increments user_failures, and logs as an error rather than being silently skipped as intended. Failure counts are inflated and genuine errors become indistinguishable from emailless-user skips.
findings.recommendation: Change the early return to 'return counts, None' to match the 2-tuple contract; then in run() add a guard before _reconcile_memberships: 'if db_user is None: continue' (already needed for the create path, CR-008).

findings.title: Newly created users skip membership sync on first run
findings.problem: After user_repository.create(), db_user remains None (it is never re-fetched from the DB). _reconcile_user returns (counts, None); run() passes None to _reconcile_memberships, which returns zeros immediately at the 'if user_db is None' guard on line 130.
findings.impact: Every user created by the sync has no project memberships applied until the next scheduled run. First-run syncs appear successful but leave new users membership-less for up to one full schedule interval.
findings.recommendation: After user_repository.create(), re-fetch the created user: db_user = await self._deps.user_repository.get_by_email(session, email) so that _reconcile_memberships receives a live user object on the same run.

findings.title: Reactivation branch discards concurrent profile field changes
findings.problem: The reactivation path calls user_repository.update(session, db_user.id, {"is_active": True}) with only is_active. If the reactivated user also has a changed name, picture, or platform_admin in Keycloak, those changes are not applied.
findings.impact: Reactivated users retain stale profile fields until the subsequent sync run. The window between reactivation and profile correction may span minutes to hours depending on the CronJob schedule.
findings.recommendation: Compute the full profile update diff (as in the else branch at lines 107-119) and merge it into the reactivation update dict: {"is_active": True, **profile_updates}. Call update once with all changed fields.

findings.title: Email field never included in user update diff
findings.problem: The update-diff logic at lines 108-113 checks name, picture, and platform_admin but never adds email to the updates dict. Spec requires updating name, email, picture, platform_admin if any field differs.
findings.impact: If a user's email changes in Keycloak (e.g. domain rename, normalisation), the platform record is never corrected. The user's old email persists in the DB while KC holds the new one, causing identity mismatch on all subsequent email-keyed lookups.
findings.recommendation: Add email to the diff check: 'if db_user.email != email: updates["email"] = email' in the update block.

findings.title: Project-admin flag never updated on existing memberships
findings.problem: _reconcile_memberships adds missing UserProject rows and removes stale ones but has no code to update the is_project_admin flag on an already-existing membership. Spec requires 'apply project-admin flag changes' as part of the membership upsert.
findings.impact: If a user's project-admin status changes in Keycloak, the platform membership retains the old flag indefinitely. Existing members may have elevated or stripped admin rights that no longer reflect their Keycloak role.
findings.recommendation: After building to_add/to_remove, also compute flag_updates: existing memberships whose is_project_admin differs from the KC group's admin attribute. Call user_project_repository.update() on each.

findings.title: budgets_synced counter incremented in dry-run mode
findings.problem: counts["budgets_synced"] += 1 is at line 161, outside the 'if not dry_run:' block. It is incremented for every membership addition regardless of whether the dry_run flag is set.
findings.impact: Dry-run summary overstates what would be written. Operators relying on dry-run output to estimate production impact will see inflated budgets_synced counts.
findings.recommendation: Move counts["budgets_synced"] += 1 inside the 'if not dry_run:' block, alongside the _sync_budget call at lines 153-157.

findings.title: DB integrity error aborts shared session, cascading failures to entire batch
findings.problem: All users in a batch share one SQLAlchemy async session (lines 203-222). An IntegrityError or any DB-level exception inside the per-user try/except leaves the session in an aborted state. Every subsequent user in the batch fails regardless of their data quality.
findings.impact: A single bad KC user record silently fails the entire remaining batch. The session.commit() at line 222 rolls back any partial work. Large batches with one bad record near the start lose all reconciliation.
findings.recommendation: Wrap each user's DB operations in a savepoint: 'async with session.begin_nested() as sp:' inside the per-user try block, with 'await sp.rollback()' in the except. This isolates individual failures without contaminating the parent session.

findings.title: KEYCLOAK_SYNC_ENABLED config var ignored by entrypoint
findings.problem: main() proceeds directly to run the sync without checking config.KEYCLOAK_SYNC_ENABLED. The CronJob hardcodes KEYCLOAK_SYNC_ENABLED: 'true', making the flag irrelevant in production deployments.
findings.impact: No runtime kill-switch for the sync outside of deleting or disabling the CronJob. Operators expecting to disable the sync temporarily by changing the env var will find it has no effect.
findings.recommendation: Add an early exit at the top of main(): 'if not config.KEYCLOAK_SYNC_ENABLED: logger.info("sync disabled by config"); return' — before _validate_env() so disabled mode requires no Keycloak credentials.

findings.title: Sync error exit path is dead code; KC-unreachable exits 0
findings.problem: coordinator.run() only ever returns SyncResult(status='ok') or SyncResult(status='skipped'); there is no code path that returns SyncResult(status='error'). The 'if result.status == "error": raise SystemExit(1)' check at line 84 is unreachable. KC-unreachable returns status='skipped' and exits 0.
findings.impact: Keycloak outages and empty-response conditions produce silent no-ops with exit code 0. backoffLimit: 2 never retries on KC failure. Monitoring alerts based on job failure counts miss these events. The named error exit contract is broken.
findings.recommendation: Add a SyncResult(status='error') return path in coordinator.run() for unrecoverable infrastructure errors (e.g. DB connection failure). In entrypoint.main(), also distinguish KC-unreachable skips (exit 1 or a separate exit code) from lock-held skips (exit 0).

findings.title: IDP mutation lock bypassed on five unguarded endpoints
findings.problem: update_user_project_assignment (PUT /projects/{projectName}/assignment/{userId}) and remove_user_from_project (DELETE /projects/{projectName}/assignment/{userId}) in projects.py have no require_no_idp_lock dependency. In user_management_router.py, bulk_set_user_budgets (PUT /budgets/bulk), reset_user_budget_spending (POST /{user_id}/budgets/reset), and set_user_budgets (PUT /{user_id}/budgets) are also unguarded. The require_no_idp_lock docstring explicitly states 'Never applied to budget-only endpoints', contradicting the spec.
findings.impact: When IDP_MANAGED_ENABLED=True, these five endpoints allow membership and budget mutations that should be IDP-controlled. Project membership state managed by Keycloak can be overwritten by direct API calls, defeating the IDP-managed regime entirely.
findings.recommendation: Add '__: None = Depends(require_no_idp_lock)' to all five handlers. Remove the 'Never applied to budget-only endpoints' note from the docstring. Add 403 tests for each endpoint. Also verify whether any additional routes in other routers are missing the guard.

findings.title: execute_request return type change breaks existing LangChain callers
findings.problem: execute_request now returns Any (response.json() for JSON responses, response.text otherwise). The existing _request method always returned str. KeycloakTool.execute() in tools.py passes through whatever execute_request returns; its declared return type is str but now receives dict/list for JSON-body endpoints.
findings.impact: LangChain agent calls that invoke KeycloakTool on JSON endpoints (including /users) receive a dict or list instead of a serialised string. Subsequent string operations (strip, split, format) on the result raise AttributeError. No existing test covers this path.
findings.recommendation: Option A: always return response.text from execute_request (matching _request) and let list_users call response.json() on the string itself. Option B: update tools.py execute() to serialise Any back to a JSON string: 'return json.dumps(result) if not isinstance(result, str) else result'.

findings.title: list_users pagination has no hard upper bound
findings.problem: The while True loop in list_users has no maximum page or user count ceiling. A misbehaving or replayed Keycloak server that always returns a non-empty page produces an unbounded loop.
findings.impact: The sync pod exhausts memory (OOM kill) or runs indefinitely. concurrencyPolicy: Forbid prevents subsequent scheduled invocations for the entire duration, effectively stopping all future syncs.
findings.recommendation: Add a hard limit: track total users fetched and raise ToolException if the count exceeds a configurable MAX_USERS ceiling (e.g. 100,000). Pass this as a parameter from coordinator.run().

findings.title: Keycloak enabled filter silently ignored due to Python bool serialisation
findings.problem: list_users passes params={"enabled": True} (Python bool) to execute_request, which forwards it to httpx as a query parameter. httpx serialises Python True as the string 'True' (capital T); Keycloak's REST API requires lowercase 'enabled=true' and silently ignores the malformed value.
findings.impact: Keycloak returns all users including disabled accounts. Disabled users are synced into the platform, potentially reactivating accounts that were intentionally disabled in KC and causing IDP-managed memberships to diverge from intended state.
findings.recommendation: Pass the value as a lowercase string: params={"enabled": "true"} (or str(True).lower()). Add a test that asserts the GET /users request is issued with enabled=true (lowercase).

findings.title: Non-list Keycloak /users response corrupts pagination loop
findings.problem: After execute_request returns, list_users checks 'if not page: break' — a non-empty dict or string is truthy and does not break the loop. users.extend(page) then iterates over dict keys (strings), not user objects. first += len(page) advances by the number of dict keys rather than user count.
findings.impact: The sync processes garbage records (dict key strings treated as user dicts), the loop may not terminate on a consistently misbehaving server, and coordinator.run() receives a list of strings causing AttributeError on kc_user.get(...) for every element.
findings.recommendation: Add a type assertion after each execute_request call: 'if not isinstance(page, list): raise ToolException(f"Expected list from /users, got {type(page).__name__}")'

findings.title: Two spec-required coordinator test cases are absent
findings.problem: Two test scenarios required by the spec are missing: (1) idempotent run — no test verifies that when a user's fields and memberships already exactly match Keycloak, zero DB write calls are issued; (2) all-four-fields update — test_reconcile_updates_changed_fields only exercises a name change; no test changes picture, platform_admin, or email in isolation or combination.
findings.impact: The idempotency invariant and the email/picture/platform_admin update paths are entirely unverified. A regression in any of those paths (including the email-missing bug in CR-010) would not be caught by the existing test suite.
findings.recommendation: Add test_reconcile_is_idempotent asserting zero calls to user_repository.update and zero calls to user_project_repository.create/delete when KC and DB are already in sync. Add test_reconcile_updates_all_profile_fields parameterised over name, email, picture, and platform_admin changes.
